title: Precomputing NPV coefficients by start year

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Project R costs 300 and then 500 in its two years of work, has no benefit in this question, and may start in 2028 or 2029. The valuation date is the start of 2027 and the rate is 5%. Which expression is the cost part of R's coefficient for a 2029 start?

options.text: 300/1.05^2 + 500/1.05^3, the two payments placed in 2029 and 2030
options.says: Right: a 2029 start pays 300 in 2029 and 500 in 2030, discounted 2 and 3 years from 2027.

options.text: 300 + 500/1.05, the two payments counted from the 2029 start
options.says: That values the start from its own year, which the page shows hides the cost of delay; the date is 2027 for every entry.

options.text: 300/1.05 + 500/1.05^2, the two payments placed in 2028 and 2029
options.says: Those are the years of a 2028 start; the profile moves with the start, so a 2029 start pays in 2029 and 2030.

options.text: (300 + 500)/1.05^2, both payments placed in the 2029 start year
options.says: Each year's cost lands in its own calendar year t + k, as in lesson 6.4.2; lumping it in the start year misplaces the 500.

origin.section: A Start-Year Coefficient Is the Project's Cash Flow, Shifted to Start in That Year

questions.stem: A plan covers 2027 to 2031. A new feeder costs $1,000k in 2030, its only year of work, and then saves $150k a year for 30 years. The table builder counts only cash flows up to 2031. What happens to the feeder's 2030 entry?

options.text: It is right, since years after 2031 hold none of the plan's decisions
options.says: The horizon limits when decisions are made, not which consequences count; the page counts every cash flow the decision causes.

options.text: It is too high, since a late start is credited with a full life of savings
options.says: Cutting at 2031 credits fewer years, not a full life; the page's 2030 relining keeps none of its 25 benefit years.

options.text: It is too low, since only the first year of its savings is counted
options.says: Right: savings start in 2031, so the cut keeps one of thirty years; the page shows the same end effect turning a $146k project into a loss.

options.text: It is unchanged, since discounting removes the far years in any case
options.says: Far years shrink but do not vanish; the page's relining is worth $119k over its life and a loss when cut.

origin.section: Count Benefits to the End of the Asset's Life, Not the End of the Plan

questions.stem: Finance lowers the discount rate from 7% to 3% for GridCap small. Which parts of lesson 6.4's start-year model change?

options.text: The budget rows, since every yearly budget is discounted at the new rate
options.says: The rate appears in no constraint; budgets are amounts per calendar year.

options.text: Only the objective's coefficients, since the rate lives in the npv table
options.says: Right: the page says the rate is inside the parameters npv[i,t] and nowhere else.

options.text: The start variables, since each start year is weighted by its discount
options.says: The variables are the same binaries x[i,t]; only their coefficients in the objective change.

options.text: Nothing at all, since the page's plan was the same at both rates
options.says: Every coefficient changes; the plan happened not to move, but the NPV went from $24,260k to $25,300k.

origin.section: The Rate Reaches the Plan Only Through the Coefficients

concepts: what a table builder that stops at the plan's last year does to late long-lived work
which parts of the timing model a new discount rate touches
which discounted terms make up one start's cost
the discount rate enters the MILP only through the objective coefficients
